correctness.rationale: The Gaussian crossing-quadratic identity is obtained via weak Gaussian integration by parts and yields the exact projected covariance. Projection completion of squares, explicit geometric sums, n=7–9 exact rationals, and a strict n>=10 bound prove two finite roots for n>=7. A cancellation identity and exact distance moment sums Q_n=2(n²-1)/3 and S_n=(n²-1)(3n²-5n+8)/30, with uniform Taylor bounds, prove both boundary scales. The existence of root sequences uses continuity, not unproved uniqueness. Extracted standalone exact-rational verifier passes 65 two-form comparisons, 3 negative-case identities and 23 distance identities; finite tests alone are not infinite proofs.

value.rationale: The dependence between the local sign-change count and global centered amplitude statistic is a motivated joint feature of stationary Gaussian time series. Centering introduces a nonlocal subtraction and unexpected covariance reversal: positive near independence and near perfect persistence but negative in between for all n>=7. Two sharply different transition widths 1/n and 1/n² and new constants 1 and 20/3 constitute a global dependence-phase theorem rather than an arbitrary parameter slice; no uniqueness/nonlinear-prediction significance is claimed.
